notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 68. My research tool refused every request, saying I had no calls left, so I never opened a single page from the sites you listed.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Without any pages, anything I wrote would come from my own memory, which your rules forbid. So I've left the notes blank rather than guess.

If you start a new session or try again, these are the pages I would read first for each part of the request:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** the Psalm 68 commentary on enduringword.com and on preceptaustin.org, and the verse pages on biblehub.com (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary). Biblehub's page for v. 18 matters most, because Paul quotes that verse in Ephesians 4:8.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** pages on how Paul uses v. 18 in Ephesians 4:8 from gotquestions.org, ligonier.org, desiringgod.org and wesley.nnu.edu. The Lutheran view would come from lcms.org and 1517.org, and the Pentecostal view of "gifts" from enduringword.com and samstorms.org.
- **Other views:**
  - **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes. They cover the hard verses (vv. 4, 11–14, 18 and 30) and the "rides on the clouds" wording in v. 4.
  - **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org, where the psalm is numbered 67.
  - **Popular modern teaching:** any discussion of v. 19 ("daily bears our burden," which some translations render "daily loads us with benefits") in prosperity-teaching debates.
